slice S4 commits (1) and (3): the readiness refusal and the seed-probe refusal become FrameworkErrors carrying surf's own code and the classified outcome, so a page_login refusal and a runtime that never started stop rendering identically (adjudication claim 45); probes carry their outcome; the links emptiness declaration replaces the bare --allow-empty. Scheduled shrink: S6 turns explore into a step list over Session.

slice S4 commit (3): SURF_EXPLORE_LINKS_EMPTINESS as a named declaration threaded through runMapped/runMappedOrThrow (the bare --allow-empty flag told surf to permit zero rows but left the framework with no record of who permitted it), and 'empty' removed from the settled readiness states because this operation passes no --empty-text marker, so surf's 'empty' is an undeclared emptiness and the page is refused rather than probed. Most of the growth is the contract documentation of those two rules. Scheduled shrink: S6 turns explore into a step list over Session. Final size includes the formatter's line breaks.

slice S4 commit (3): HealingFinding carries the typed outcome basis and isHealableFinding gates selector extraction on basis 'fault', so a no_evidence, contradiction or indeterminate finding no longer drives a selector rewrite while unclassified legacy findings keep healing (result-classification packet refinement; adjudication axiom A7). Scheduled shrink: the healer's strategy list moves behind the ReceiptStore seam in S5.

slice S5 commit (3): run(context?) takes the kernel RunContext and threads it to every agent so a nested explore shares one run id, one ledger and one receipt store (architecture review A5, adjudication claim 1); a library caller that passes none still gets one minted from the parsed config, so a mutating agent can never run outside the ledger; TestResult gains the redacted mutations[] of the run. Scheduled shrink: correlation, root cause and propagation move to a diagnosis consumer (architecture adjudication Part 4).

slice S5 commit (3): the operation declares SURF_EXPLORE_OPERATION_EFFECT (read_only with browser_session scope, because explore owns the tab it opens), takes the RunContext through to executeSurfExploreOperation so the surf agent's nested explore shares the run, and returns through finalizeEnvelope carrying its own class (a nested explore reports the run of its parent and the class of itself). Scheduled shrink: S6 turns explore into a step list over Session.

slice S5 commit (4): healing writes become conditional EffectSteps on the kernel ledger (mutation-safety packet, refinement 5 and 6). analyzeFile stamps the sha256 of the content a proposal was made against, applyProposals runs one step per file keyed sha256(file | before-hash | change) with that hash as the precondition re-read immediately before the rename, the after-hash read-back is the step's verify, a rename that threw settles `unknown` rather than `failed` (settleHealWrite), and the restore path becomes compensation steps that run only for a sibling whose own receipt says `applied`. Most of the growth is the compensate() method and the contract documentation of those rules. Scheduled shrink: the healer's strategy list and the write path split when heal becomes a step list over the session (post-S6).

slice S6 commit (2): the scheduled shrink. explorePage becomes a step list over the kernel Session (architecture review A8, adjudication claim 22), so the runtime resolution, the owned-tab lifecycle, the readiness gate and surf's readiness vocabulary leave this file for src/core/surf-session.ts and src/core/surf-readiness.ts. What stays is what explore alone knows: the probe expressions, the evidence assertion, link extraction, coverage and the envelope. Still over the 700-line budget; the next shrink is the probe/coverage split once S8 adds frameRootCause to the probe shape.

slice S7 commit (1): the explore input schema gains a preprocess step that checks the *raw* input for the submit gate's options. The three surf actions share one commander command, so `--field`, `--out`, `--plan`, `--submit` and `--confirm-plan` arrive here too, and a key explore does not declare would be stripped by zod before anything could refuse it - which is how an operator's fill options would be silently ignored by a read-only explore. Scheduled shrink: the probe/coverage split named in the S6 entry, once S8 adds frameRootCause to the probe shape.

slice S7 commit (2): translateSurfArgs teaches `click`, `type` and `select` to carry `--tab-id`. It is a *global* surf option, so the three value-setting verbs accept it even though their own --help does not list it, and without it the session refuses them under the owned-tab rule - a submit would otherwise act on whichever tab the browser has in front. Eight lines: one value flag and one passthrough per verb. Scheduled shrink: the argv translation table moves behind the adapter's translate() seam once a second adapter needs one.

slice S7, from the live dogfood: `--no-screenshot` is accepted and forwarded for `type`, `select`, `click` and `js`. The surf build saves a screenshot of the page to /tmp after every value-setting verb and after every `js` call, which is a copy of the value that was just typed, outside the 0600 artifacts the packet's A10 rule is about (submit-gate packet §8; measured live 2026-09-08: four screenshots per fill run before the flag, none after). Twenty-four lines: the flag constant, one helper, and one bool-flag plus passthrough per verb. Scheduled shrink: the argv translation table moves behind the adapter's translate() seam once a second adapter needs one.

slice S8 commit (2): --ready-selector puts a selector into the readiness gate, which is the run's first way to fail to reach an element, and --frame-hint is the only v1 route to a confirmed frame determination. What lands here is the option pair (schema, the refusal of a hint with no selector to fail on), the call into Session.explainUnreachable while the tab is still open, and probes[].frameRootCause on the failed page; the step list, the classifier and the error carrier live in src/core/frame-diagnosis.ts and src/core/frame-root-cause.ts. Scheduled shrink: the probe/coverage split named in the S6 entry, now that the probe shape carries frameRootCause.
